effects.prompt: Destroy a Lightning Flow you control? (If you do, Astral Assault gets +2{p}.)

_comment: 'When this attacks, you may destroy a Lightning Flow you control. If you do, this gets +2{p}.' Release note: the trigger fires when this resolves onto the combat chain - ON_ATTACK on an Action - Attack card, the shipped pound_town_blue / rising_knee_thrust shape. The whole clause is MAY's all-or-nothing block: destroy + pump sit together in effects, so declining runs neither and 'if you do' needs no plumbing. The MAY's conditions gate whether the prompt is offered at all (loader pops them into an effect-level gate; with no else block that is exactly 'no legal target, nothing happens'), which is the usage CONTROLS_SUBTYPE's docstring blesses for 'destroy an X ... if you do' clauses. Two data facts drove the type choices, both verified: Lightning Flow exists in the corpus ONLY as a token (json/tokens/lightning_flow.json) whose card-DB subtypes are ['Aura'] - it has NO 'Lightning Flow' subtype - so CONTROLS_SUBTYPE/DESTROY_PERMANENT-by-subtype would never match; hence CONTROLS_TOKEN_TYPE (matches by slug, condition_types.py ~1697) for the gate. For the destroy I chose DESTROY_MATCHING with an explicit object target (zone ARENA = permanents, name flat-matches 'Lightning Flow') over the triage's alternate DESTROY_TOKEN because DESTROY_TOKEN destroys the FIRST matching token with no player choice, while 'a Lightning Flow' with several in play implies the controller picks; _compile_object_target asks. Known minor infidelity: with exactly one flow the destroy path still prompts (single-option ask) - cosmetic only. MODIFY_ATTACK add 2 on a one-shot ON_ATTACK trigger records into combat.power_mods and survives later recalculations (effect_types.py ~4081 cites this exact Reckless-Arithmetic pattern). No known gaps.
